_about: Hand-labelled evaluation set for retrieval quality.
Each entry is a mood query plus titles a human considers clearly relevant.
HOW THESE LABELS WERE MADE (this matters for reading the numbers):
First written from memory, then extended by POOLING -- running the retriever and
judging its top-5 by hand, adding the ones that are genuinely relevant. Pooling is
the standard IR practice (TREC works this way) because nobody can label 912 titles
per query. Its bias is equally standard: a title no system ever surfaces never gets
judged, so the absolute score is OPTIMISTIC. Only the DELTA between two runs of the
The first run made the case for it vividly: 'mind-bending science fiction' scored
recall 0.00 while returning Black Mirror, Eternal Sunshine, The Prestige and
Westworld -- an excellent result the labels simply did not know about. It also
exposed two labels ('Alien', 'The Road') that are not in the catalogue at all, and
two wrong ones (Wolf of Wall Street / Django Unchained as 'mafia' films).
Known limits: small (12 queries), single annotator, biased towards well-known
titles. Every label must exist in the index or it can never be retrieved --
scripts/evaluate_retrieval.py checks that before spending any quota.
